name: Singju
instructions: 1. Finely slice the lotus stem, banana stem, and other seasonal vegetables.
2. Dry roast the perilla seeds until aromatic and grind them into a coarse powder.
3. Mash the fermented fish (ngari) with fresh green chilies, ginger, and salt to create a spicy paste.
4. Combine the sliced vegetables, perilla powder, and the ngari paste in a large mixing bowl.
5. Add a dash of roasted chickpea flour for texture and garnish with fresh chives and coriander.
6. Toss well by hand to ensure all ingredients are coated evenly before serving immediately.
description: Singju is a quintessential Manipuri street food salad. It is deeply embedded in the social fabric of the state, often enjoyed as a refreshing snack during afternoon gatherings. While vegetarian versions exist, the authentic traditional preparation incorporates fermented fish (ngari), which gives the dish its signature bold and pungent umami flavor profile.
